sections.title: Tree and identifying features
sections.text: Field elm is a deciduous tree that may reach around 30 m, though smaller forms are common. Its oval, doubly toothed leaves have an uneven leaf base; clusters of small flowers open before the leaves, followed by flat, roundish winged fruits (samaras). The plate matches these features.

sections.title: Range and food
sections.text: It is native from Europe across parts of Central Asia and North Africa. Young samaras have been eaten locally, but this is not a general food recommendation; no toxicological safety claim is made here.
